results.title: Chapter: 4 Barriers to Representation of Underrepresented ...
results.content: Attitudes of 204 Black men about a variety of types of clinical research, including surveys, focus groups, clinical trials, and genetic studies, found that 74 percent endorsed a willingness to participate (Byrd et al., 2011). In a clinical trial exploring barriers and motivators to participation in clinical trials among 67 Black Americans, focus group themes included the perception that research would benefit white participants or the research institution more so than any underrepresented individuals enrolling in the study (BeLue et al., 2006). Engaging patients, community members, or other stakeholders in research has been identified as a useful strategy for enhancing participation of underrepresented groups in the research process and, ultimately, reducing health inequalities and improving population health outcomes (Nguyen et al., 2021). In one systematic review of clinical research studies, patient and community involvement in designing recruitment and retention strategies, developing patient-facing information, helping to identify potential participants, or providing feedback on poor recruitment rates was associated with higher odds of a patient enrolling in a clinical trial (Crocker et al., 2018).
